meta.name: Carrier rules dataset: dated rule changes
meta.source_policy: Every value comes from the carrier's or the seller's own page or PDF. Each section lists its sources.
meta.units: Lengths in inches, volumes in cubic inches, weights in pounds, divisors in in³/lb or cm³/kg, money in USD.
meta.warning: Carriers change rules, usually in January and July. Check the source before you rely on a value.

changes.title: Dimensional weight divisor cut from 166 to 139
changes.summary: Applies to Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, USPS Ground Advantage and Parcel Select, at both retail and commercial prices. The 1,728 in³ threshold below which USPS charges actual weight did not change.

sources.title: USPS Postal Bulletin 22705 — DMM Revision: dimensional weight
USPS DMM 223 (Priority Mail: DIM weight, cubic, nonstandard fees)

changes.title: 3.5% fuel and logistics surcharge applied to FBA fees
changes.summary: Applies to FBA in the US and Canada and to Remote Fulfillment with FBA. It is a percentage on the fulfilment fee, not a change to a size tier or divisor.

sources.title: Amazon — 2026 US FBA fulfillment fee changes

changes.title: 2026 US fulfilment fee changes take effect
changes.summary: Fee amounts and weight bands change; the size tier definitions and the ÷139 dimensional weight rule did not.

Amazon — 2026 US referral and FBA fee changes summary

changes.title: 2026 Service Guide and surcharge changes take effect
changes.summary: Additional Handling — Dimension and Oversize amounts rise. The size thresholds that trigger them did not change.

changes.title: Each fraction of an inch rounds up to the next whole inch
changes.summary: UPS announced this on its shipping costs page before the change. Its example: “if the length of a package is 11.1 inches, that package will be deemed to have a length of 12 inches”. The change started on 18 August 2025, the same day as the FedEx change. Before it, UPS rounded each measurement to the nearest whole number. The guide effective 23 December 2024 reads “1.00 to 1.49 will be considered 1”. The 2026 guide reads as quoted.
